newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Electronics push Taiwan stocks past 9,022 threshold.
newsitem.headline: Electronics push Taiwan stocks past 9,022 threshold.

text.p: Taiwan share prices opened higher on Thursday, pushing past a seven-year intraday high of 9,021.87 points as the recently volatile electronics regrouped to lead the upward momentum, brokers said.
After 39 minutes at 0139 GMT, the index was up 73.90 points or 0.83 percent at 9,030.31. Turnover was T$67 billion.
Electronics were up 2.28 percent, with chipmaker Winbond up T$3.5 to T$58.5 after it said it was considering a huge wafer project worth around T$160 billion.
"The repeated huge investment plans in the semiconductor industry further supports the expected sound outlook of the industry," said indepedent analyst Michael Hung.

Taiwan's top two chipmakers, Taiwan Semiconductor and United Microelectronics, have announced even bigger long-range wafer fab ventures since April, bolstering Taiwan's most important industrial sector.
Brokers warned that investors would be cautious after the finance ministry said on Wednesday it had no immediate plans to raise the ceiling on foreign ownership of Taiwan stocks.
"The actual killing power (of the ministry move) is not big but it shows the government's aim of cooling down the market," Hung said.
Taiwan currently allows foreign funds to own up to 25 percent of a listed firm's total market value.

The ministry, reporting after a semiannual review, said it did not see a need for further liberalisation because foreign investors currently hold only about four percent of the stock market value despite its recent torrid bull run.
